concepts.label: vtep-binding
concepts.gloss: A vtep-binding is the attachment record that realizes an overlay segment by mapping a specific VNI (overlay-segment) onto a particular VTEP node so that that VTEP will encapsulate/decapsulate traffic for that VNI.
concepts.example: bind-vtep3-50201: the binding that maps vni-50201 (tenant-blue) onto the VTEP node vtep-leaf3, i.e., vtep-leaf3 will advertise and terminate tunnels for VNI 50201.

concepts.label: overlay-segment
concepts.gloss: An overlay-segment is a logical Layer‑2 domain identified by a VNI that carries a tenant's L2 traffic across the overlay and is realized on the fabric by one or more vtep-bindings.
concepts.example: vni-50201 (tenant-blue): a tenant-blue Layer‑2 network identified by VNI 50201 that is realized when one or more bindings (e.g., bind-vtep3-50201) are present on VTEPs.

concepts.label: vtep-node
concepts.gloss: A vtep-node is a physical or virtual switch/router that hosts VTEP bindings and terminates/initiates overlay tunnels (it 'hosts' vtep-binding attachments for VNIs).
concepts.example: vtep-leaf3: a leaf switch acting as a VTEP which hosts the binding bind-vtep3-50201 so that it encapsulates/decapsulates traffic for vni-50201.

concepts.label: overlay-mtu
concepts.gloss: An overlay-mtu is the framing constraint (MTU) applied to an overlay segment that defines the maximum payload size allowed inside the encapsulated tunnels for that VNI.
concepts.example: MTU 9216 required: vni-50201 is configured with a required MTU of 9216 to ensure host-to-host packets fit inside VXLAN/GPE encapsulation without fragmentation.

concepts.label: anycast-gateway
concepts.gloss: An anycast-gateway is a distributed Layer‑3 gateway address configured for an overlay-segment so that multiple VTEPs present the same default-gateway IP locally for hosts in that VNI.
concepts.example: anycast-gw 10.20.1.1: the IP 10.20.1.1 is programmed on all VTEPs serving vni-50201 so hosts use the same local gateway while routing is distributed.

concepts.label: microseg-policy
concepts.gloss: A microseg-policy is a micro‑segmentation policy that defines groups, selectors and enforcement rules (ACLs/filters) applied to an overlay-segment to control east‑west traffic between endpoints in that VNI.
concepts.example: policy-blue-web-app: a policy applied to vni-50201 that permits HTTP/HTTPS between web-tier endpoints and denies other lateral access according to the microsegmentation rules.

concepts.label: security-zone
concepts.gloss: A security-zone is a named policy-group or zone used to collect endpoints or segments under the same security semantics; zones are grouped by microseg-policies to apply common rules to those collections.
concepts.example: zone-dmz: a security zone containing public-facing servers in vni-50201 that is associated with policy-blue-web-app to enforce DMZ access controls.

concepts.label: vertex-tag-6
concepts.gloss: Vertex-tag-6 is a vendor‑specific opaque attribute attached to an overlay-segment (VNI) used for proprietary metadata, special forwarding or feature flags that the controller and devices interpret internally.
concepts.example: vertex-tag-6=0x1 on vni-50201: the proprietary tag value 0x1 applied to vni-50201 indicating a vendor-specific handling mode (e.g., enhanced telemetry or special forwarding) on all VTEPs serving that VNI.
